source_note: Compiled from official notices and mainstream reporting. Every card links to its original source.

items.title: US warns EB-1 green card category for Indians may run out before September 30
items.summary: The United States has issued an alert that the EB-1 green card category may be exhausted before the end of September. This affects Indian applicants seeking permanent residence through the employment-based first preference route, which typically serves priority workers.

items.title: UK immigration rules changing from October: Five major updates announced
items.summary: The United Kingdom is implementing changes to its immigration rules starting in October. Five significant modifications have been announced that will affect visa applicants. Indian nationals planning to travel, work or study in the UK should review these upcoming rule changes.

items.title: Canada study permit 2026: Higher financial requirements and tighter scrutiny ahead
items.summary: Canada is introducing changes to study permit requirements in 2026, including increased proof of funds and stricter application review processes. Indian students planning to study in Canada will need to demonstrate higher financial capacity and face more rigorous assessment of their applications.

items.title: US reportedly weighing H-1B changes including grace period and H-4 work authorization
items.summary: The United States is reportedly considering modifications to H-1B visa rules that could affect grace periods for job changes, fee structures and employment authorization for H-4 dependent visa holders. These potential changes would impact Indian workers and their families in America.

items.title: How Indians on US tourist visas can extend their stay using Form I-539
items.summary: Indians visiting the United States on tourist visas can apply to extend their stay by submitting Form I-539. The article explains the application process, timing requirements and what this form means for visitors seeking to remain in the country beyond their initial authorized period.

items.title: Trump administration reportedly considering stricter H-1B and student visa rules
items.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly weighing tighter restrictions on H-1B work visas, green cards and student visas. These potential policy changes could significantly impact Indian nationals seeking to work or study in the United States, though no final decisions have been confirmed.

items.title: Can Indians work in Canada on a visitor visa? Rules on jobs and penalties explained
items.summary: The article clarifies Canadian regulations regarding employment on visitor visas. It explains what work is permitted, when separate work permits are required, and the penalties Indians may face for working illegally while in Canada on visitor status without proper authorization.

items.title: UK student visa fees increasing from November 2026 for Indian applicants
items.summary: The cost of obtaining a UK student visa will rise starting November 2026. Indian students planning to study in the United Kingdom need to factor in these higher fees when budgeting for their education abroad and preparing their visa applications.

items.title: UAE Golden Visa eligibility: What Indians need to know about the ₹5 crore threshold
items.summary: The article examines whether an investment of five crore rupees qualifies Indians for the UAE Golden Visa programme. It covers eligibility criteria, rules and benefits of this long-term residency scheme for investors and professionals seeking to settle in the Emirates.

items.title: H-1B visa fees could exceed $200,000 under reported Trump administration proposal
items.summary: A proposal under consideration by the Trump administration could raise H-1B visa fees to over two hundred thousand dollars. This potential increase would significantly impact Indian tech workers and their employers who sponsor these employment-based visas, though the change is not yet confirmed.

items.title: September 2026 Visa Bulletin warns some categories may run out before 30 September
items.summary: The US State Department has kept employment-based final action dates unchanged for September, but cautioned that EB-1 India, EB-2 and unreserved EB-5 could retrogress or become unavailable as annual limits are reached before the fiscal year closes. EB-2 remains unavailable for applicants born in India. Anyone whose date is current should be filing now rather than waiting.

items.title: New public charge standard from 18 September, immigrant visa interviews paused for officer training
items.summary: USCIS form changes tied to a new public charge standard take effect on 18 September 2026. Separately, the State Department is temporarily pausing immigrant visa interview appointments worldwide while consular officers are trained on the new screening guidance. Applicants with scheduled interviews should watch for rescheduling notices rather than assume their date holds.

items.title: Family-sponsored cut-off dates advance sharply, some by more than two years
items.summary: Several family-sponsored categories moved forward significantly in the September bulletin, with advances of over two years in some cases. The department has attributed the movement to reduced immigrant visa issuance for certain nationalities. Practitioners note that consular capacity in the final month may limit how many of those numbers actually get used.

items.title: Express Entry keeps favouring category-based draws in shortage occupations
items.summary: Canada's Express Entry system continues to run category-based selection rounds aimed at healthcare, science and technology, engineering and skilled trades, rather than relying only on general draws. With Indian applicant volumes high, CRS scores have stayed competitive — most candidates are responding by improving language scores and documenting work experience more carefully.

items.title: UK keeps tighter dependant rules for several student categories
items.summary: The UK continues to restrict dependant visas for certain categories of international students as part of a wider migration control effort. Indian numbers remain strong regardless — the sponsored study visa acceptance rate for Indian applicants has been reported around 97 per cent. Post-study employment increasingly depends on a genuine job offer at a competitive salary.
